body_text:
Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be an open set. A function $f: U \to \mathbb{C}$ is *analytic*
at a point $z_0 \in U$ if there exists an open disk $D(z_0, r) \subseteq U$ and a sequence of
coefficients $(a_n)_{n=0}^\infty$ such that:
$$ f(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n (z - z_0)^n \quad \text{for all } z \in D(z_0, r). $$
A function is analytic on $U$ if it is analytic at every point of $U$.

By term-by-term differentiation, the coefficients are uniquely determined by the higher derivatives
of $f$ evaluated at the center:
$$ a_n = \frac{f^{(n)}(z_0)}{n!}. $$
